body:
OK - it seems that my reproduction case was not correct, my apologies. I have just done this from fresh and can confirm that this exhibits the incorrect behaviour I described:

create a new AWS lambda project using the instructions at  https://quarkus.io/guides/aws-lambda. Create the project using the maven archetype:

`mvn archetype:generate \
       -DarchetypeGroupId=io.quarkus \
       -DarchetypeArtifactId=quarkus-amazon-lambda-archetype \
       -DarchetypeVersion=3.29.3`

...and enter the values below when prompted:
Define value for property 'groupId': `org.example`
Define value for property 'artifactId': `getting-started`
Define value for property 'version' 1.0-SNAPSHOT: (ENTER to accept the default)
Define value for property 'package' org.example: (ENTER to accept the default)

Now, in the src/test/resources/application.properties file add:
`quarkus.http.test-timeout=120s` 
after the line:
`quarkus.lambda.handler=test`

Run `quarkus build`

You will then see the warning in the logs during the test execution:
`2025-11-18 10:46:00,095 WARN  [io.qua.config] (main) Unrecognized configuration key "quarkus.http.test-timeout" was provided; it will be ignored; verify that the dependency extension for this configuration is set or that you did not make a typo`

Thanks for the update. 

That happens because Quarkus Lambda does not bring in any HTTP stack

I see, but it does use the (I think) Apache HTTP stack for REST Assured and therefore I would expect to be able to set the timeout for the tests. In the trivial example project, this is not necessary, but in something more substantial the tests do not allow the lambda to run for more than 30s
The Apache HTTP Client stack is not something we manage (or even influence).

Of course, but the configuration property `quarkus.http.test-timeout` is not part of the Apache HTTP stack.
If you take a look at the information [here](https://quarkus.io/guides/getting-started-testing#controlling-http-interaction-timeout) you'll see there are no caveats given around the use of this property when using REST Assured. 
This is exactly what the test cases in the AWS Lambda project use, and therefore it is expected behaviour for this configuration parameter to be honored.

I still don't know how to fix the problem, and clearly the example project can't be configured as described in the Quarkus docs. Either the docs need to be updated to explain what a user needs to do to set that property when testing a Lambda function or the implementation needs to be fixed to allow the property to be set used by REST Assured

If the simplest 'getting started' project https://quarkus.io/guides/getting-started works correctly, then it would suggest that the Lambda project is not pulling in its dependencies properly and this should be fixed.

Not correct. The `getting-started` pulls in the HTTP layer, which is why you are seeing the difference compared to the Lambda example.
Lambda should not pull in the HTTP layer by default

But it uses REST Assured for tests so it does need to pull that
Or something needs refactoring so that config property is correctly honored by the client side HTTP stack
In any case, the warning is a false positive

issue.title: Move `quarkus.http.test-timeout` to `TestConfig`
issue.body:
This is done to overcome the false positive that
Quarkus displays when the property is set and
the `quarkus-vertx-http` extension isn't part
of the classpath.

- Closes: #51061

issue.title: Create separate `HttpTestConfig` for `quarkus.http.test-timeout`
issue.body:
Instead of moving the property to TestConfig which would result in the property path being `quarkus.test.http.test-timeout`, create a separate ConfigMapping for `quarkus.http` prefix.

- Fixes: #51061
- Supercedes: #51131
